label: thmB
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thmB}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)}]
\item Let $g\in\exp(\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_2)$. Then $P_{\rho_4}s(S_g)\in s\,\widehat U(\mathfrak{t}_4)$ if and only if $g$ has no linear term in $x$, and in that case $P_{\rho_4}s(S_g)=s(S'_g)$. Consequently
\[
\bigl\{g\in\exp(\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_2):P_{\rho_4}s(S_g)=s(S_g\,h^{1,2,3})\text{ for some }h\in\exp(\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_2')\bigr\}={\mathsf{ASTR}}\cdot\exp(\mathbb{K} y),
\]
and $h=\varphi$ when $g=\varphi\exp(\alpha y)$ with $\varphi\in{\mathsf{ASTR}}$. This is the flip equation of \cite[Theorem~78]{FHK}, without the hypothesis on the linear term in $x$. For $g\in{\mathsf{ASTR}}$ the relation $P_{\rho_4}^2=1$ gives $g(x,y)\,g(y,x)=1$.

\item Let $g\in\exp(\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_2')$. Then $\Theta_g$ commutes with the action of $\Sigma_4$ on $\mathbf{A}$ if and only if $g(x,y)\,g(y,x)=1$.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, together with Theorem~\ref{thm:classification}, $g\mapsto\Theta_g$ is a group isomorphism $({\mathsf{GRT}}_1, \circledast) \cong\operatorname{Aut}^+_{\mathbf{cyc},1}({\mathsf{PaRCD}}_{\mathbb{K}})$, for the product $\circledast$ defined in ~\eqref{eq:grouplaw}.

label: rem:grt-drinfeld
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:grt-drinfeld}
A group-like $g$ satisfying (P) has no linear terms \cite[Lemma 75(1)]{FHK}, so Definition~\ref{def:grt} agrees with \cite[Definition~73(3)]{FHK}. The map $g\mapsto g^{-1}$ carries \textup{(P)} to Drinfeld's pentagon as written in \cite{Drin,Furusho_pentagon}, and by \cite[Lemmas~6 and~9, Theorem~3]{Furusho_pentagon} it identifies ${\mathsf{GRT}}_1$ with Drinfeld's group \cite[\S5]{Drin}. Likewise ${\mathfrak{grt}}_1$ is Drinfeld's Lie algebra.
head: environment

label: rem:normalisation
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:normalisation}
The restriction to $\mathcal{F}^3$ in Definition~\ref{def:grt} cannot be dropped. For $\psi=[x,y]$ one computes in $\mathfrak{t}_4$
\[
S'_\psi-S_\psi-\psi^{1,2,3}=-[t_{01},t_{23}]-[t_{02},t_{13}]=0,
\]
so $[x,y]$ satisfies (P$'$), whereas $[x,y]+[y,z]+[z,x]=3[x,y]$ for $z=-x-y$, so it violates the linearised three-cycle relation; compare \cite[\S1]{Furusho_pentagon}. Since (P$'$) is homogeneous for the weight grading and $\mathcal{F}^2\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_2/\mathcal{F}^3\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_2=\mathbb{K} \cdot [x,y]$, it follows that
\[
\bigl\{\psi\in\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_2':\ \psi\text{ satisfies (P$'$)}\bigr\}=\mathbb{K}\cdot [x,y]\oplus{\mathfrak{grt}}_1 .
\]
In particular, the set defined in \cite[Definition~73(4)]{FHK} by the Lie-likeness condition and the linearised pentagon equation alone is $\mathbb{K}\cdot [x,y]\oplus{\mathfrak{grt}}_1$, and not ${\mathfrak{grt}}_1$.

label: def:parcd
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:parcd}
For $n\ge1$, let ${\mathsf{PaRCD}}_{\mathbb{K}}(n)$ be the groupoid with object set $\Omega(n)$, with $\operatorname{Hom}(p,q)=\exp(\mathfrak{ft}_n)$ for all $p,q$, and with composition given by multiplication: the composite of $u\colon p\to q$ followed by $v\colon q\to r$ is $uv\colon p\to r$. We write a morphism as $(u\colon p\to q)$ and call $u$ its \emph{coefficient}. The operad structure is that of $\Omega$ on objects and that of $\widehat U(\mathfrak{ft})$ on coefficients, and $\sigma\in\Sigma_{n+1}$ acts by $\sigma$ on objects and by $P_\sigma$ on coefficients. This is the cyclic operad of \emph{parenthesized ribbon chord diagrams} \cite[\S1]{singh2026cyclic}, \cite[\S5.1]{willwacher2024cyclic}.

label: lem:tau-generators
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:tau-generators}
The transpositions $\tau_n$ act on the generators by
\[
P_{\tau_1}\mathbf{I}=\mathbf{I},\qquad P_{\tau_2}\mathbf{H}=\bigl(-T_{01}-T_{11}\ \text{at }(10)\bigr),\qquad P_{\tau_2}\mathbf{X}=\mathbf{X}^{-1},\qquad P_{\tau_3}\mathbf{A}=A_{120}^{-1}.
\]

label: thm:classification
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:classification}
For every $g\in{\mathsf{GRT}}_1$ there is a unique $\Theta_g\in\operatorname{Aut}^+_{\mathbf{Op},1}({\mathsf{PaRCD}}_{\mathbb{K}})$ with $\Theta_g(\mathbf{A})=g(T_{01},T_{12})\,\mathbf{A}$, and $g\mapsto\Theta_g$ is a bijection ${\mathsf{GRT}}_1\to\operatorname{Aut}^+_{\mathbf{Op},1}({\mathsf{PaRCD}}_{\mathbb{K}})$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Restriction to ${\mathsf{PaCD}}_{\mathbb{K}}$ is injective, as ${\mathsf{PaRCD}}_{\mathbb{K}}$ is generated by $\exp(\mathbb{K}\mathbf{I})$, $\exp(\mathbb{K}\mathbf{H})$, $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{A}$. By \cite{BN}, \cite[Section 10.3]{FresseBook1}, the restriction is the automorphism $G_g$ of ${\mathsf{PaCD}}_{\mathbb{K}}$ with $G_g(\mathbf{X})=\mathbf{X}$ and $G_g(\mathbf{A})=g(T_{01},T_{12})\mathbf{A}$, for a unique $g\in{\mathsf{GRT}}_1$. Conversely, $G_g$ fixes $\exp(\lambda s(c_k))$ at every
$p\in\Omega(k)$. Since $c_k$ is central, it suffices to take $p=(p'(k-1))$, where 
$\exp(\lambda s(c_k))=\exp(\lambda\mathbf{H})\circ_0\exp(\lambda s(c_{k-1}))$ by \eqref{eq:cabling}, so the claim follows by induction on $k$.
Using \eqref{eq:framing-splitting}, extend $G_g$ by the identity on $\mathcal{Z}_n$. By \eqref{eq:cabling},
\[
\big(s(v)e^{z}\big)\circ_a\big(s(w)e^{z'}\big)
=\big(s(v)\circ_a s(w)\big)\big(0\circ_a e^{2\mu_a s(c_k)}\big)e^{z''},
\]
where $\mu_a$ is the coefficient of $T_{aa}$ in $z$ and $z''\in Z$. Hence, the extension
is an operad automorphism preserving ${\mathsf{PaCD}}_{\mathbb{K}}$, and it is $\Theta_g$.

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:pentagonPaRCD}
Let $\Theta$ be an object-fixing continuous operad endomorphism of ${\mathsf{PaRCD}}_{\mathbb{K}}$ with $\Theta(\mathbf{A})=g(T_{01},T_{12})\mathbf{A}$ for some $g\in\exp(\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_2)$. Then $\Theta(\mathbf{A}^B)=s(g^B)\,\mathbf{A}^B$ for each of the five labels $B$ in \eqref{eq:cabledA}, and $g$ satisfies \textup{(P)}.

label: prop:reflection
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(1) For $0<i,j<n$, \eqref{eq:tau} gives $P_{\rho_n}s(t_{ij})=T_{n-i,n-j}$ with $0<n-i,n-j<n$. For $0<j<n$,
\[
P_{\rho_n}s(t_{0j})=T_{n,\,n-j}=-\sum_{\substack{k<n\\k\ne n-j}}T_{k,\,n-j}-T_{n-j,\,n-j},
\]
and the first sum is $sF_n(t_{0j})$.

(2) By \eqref{eq:framing-splitting}, $q$ is a morphism of Lie algebras, so $q P_{\rho_n}s$ is a continuous Lie algebra endomorphism of $\mathfrak{t}_n$. By (1) it is given on generators by \eqref{eq:intro-flip}. Write $F_n=qP_{\rho_n}s$. Again by \eqref{eq:framing-splitting},
\[
P_{\rho_n}s=sF_n+\zeta,
\]
where $\zeta\colon\mathfrak{t}_n\to\mathcal{Z}_n$ is a continuous Lie algebra map to an abelian Lie algebra, hence vanishes on $\mathfrak{d}_n$. By (1), $\zeta$ takes values in $\mathcal{Z}_n'=\operatorname{span}\{T_{ii}:0<i<n\}$, and $P_{\rho_n}(\mathcal{Z}_n')=\mathcal{Z}_n'\subset\ker q$ by \eqref{eq:tau}. Since $P_{\rho_n}^2=1$ and $qs=\operatorname{id}$,
\[
u=qP_{\rho_n}^2s(u)=qP_{\rho_n}\bigl(sF_n(u)+\zeta(u)\bigr)=F_n^2(u)\qquad(u\in\mathfrak{t}_n),
\]
so $F_n$ is an involutive automorphism. Finally, with $c'=\sum_{0<a<b<n}t_{ab}$ we have $F_n(c')=c'$ and
\[
F_n\Bigl(\sum_{0<m<n}t_{0m}\Bigr)=-\sum_{0<m<n}\ \sum_{k\ne m}t_{km}=-\sum_{0<m<n}t_{0m}-2c',
\]
so $F_n(c_n)=-c_n$.

(3) Since $\zeta$ vanishes on $\mathfrak{d}_n$, $P_{\rho_n}s=sF_n$ on $\mathfrak{d}_n$, and both sides are algebra maps on $\widehat U(\mathfrak{d}_n)$.
head: environment

label: prop:taylor
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:taylor}
Let $n\ge2$. Identify
\[
\widehat U(\mathfrak{ft}_n)=s\,\widehat U(\mathfrak{t}_n)\,\widehat\otimes\,\mathbb{K}[[T_{00},\dots,T_{n-1,n-1}]]
\]
via \eqref{eq:framing-splitting}, and consider the derivation
\[
D=\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}\partial_{0j}\otimes T_{n-j,n-j}.
\]
Then for every $u\in\widehat U(\mathfrak{t}_n)$
\begin{equation}\label{eq:taylor}
P_{\rho_n}s(u)=(sF_n\otimes\operatorname{id})\bigl(\exp(-D)(u\otimes1)\bigr)=\sum_{\nu\in\mathbb{N}^{n-1}}\frac{(-1)^{|\nu|}}{\nu!}\,T^\nu\,sF_n\bigl(\partial^\nu u\bigr),
\end{equation}
where $T^\nu=\prod_{j=1}^{n-1}T_{n-j,n-j}^{\nu_j}$, $\partial^\nu=\prod_{j=1}^{n-1}\partial_{0j}^{\nu_j}$ and $\nu!=\prod_j\nu_j!$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since the $T_{ii}$ are central, $D$ is a continuous derivation of
\[
\widehat U(\mathfrak{t}_n)\,\widehat\otimes\,\mathbb{K}[[T_{00},\dots,T_{n-1,n-1}]].
\]
It lowers the weight in $\widehat U(\mathfrak{t}_n)$ by one and raises the polynomial degree in the framings by one, so $\exp(-D)$ converges, and it is an algebra automorphism by the Leibniz formula for $D^k(uv)$. The map $sF_n\otimes\operatorname{id}$ is an algebra map because the framings are central. Both sides of the first equality in \eqref{eq:taylor} are therefore continuous algebra maps in $u$, and it suffices to compare them on generators. For $0<a<b<n$, $D(t_{ab})=0$ and both sides equal $sF_n(t_{ab})$. For $0<j<n$, $D(t_{0j}\otimes1)=1\otimes T_{n-j,n-j}$ and $D^2(t_{0j}\otimes 1)=0$, so the right-hand side is $sF_n(t_{0j})-T_{n-j,n-j}$, which is $P_{\rho_n}s(t_{0j})$ by \eqref{eq:defect}. The second equality follows by expanding $\exp(-D)$, the $\partial_{0j}$ commuting.
head: environment

label: cor:dagger
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:dagger}
Let $n\ge2$ and $u\in\widehat U(\mathfrak{t}_n)$. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item $P_{\rho_n}s(u)\in s\,\widehat U(\mathfrak{t}_n)$.
\item $u\in\widehat U(\mathfrak{t}_n)^\dagger$.
\item $P_{\rho_n}s(u)=sF_n(u)$.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover $\widehat U(\mathfrak{t}_n)^\dagger=\widehat U(\mathfrak{h}_n)$, and $F_n(\mathfrak{h}_n)=\mathfrak{h}_n$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The monomials $T^
u$ are linearly independent over $s\,\widehat U(\mathfrak{t}_n)$, and $
u\mapsto T^
u$ is injective. In \eqref{eq:taylor} the coefficient of $T_{n-j,n-j}$ is $-sF_n(\partial_{0j}u)$. If (i) holds, these coefficients vanish, and since $sF_n$ is injective, $\partial_{0j}u=0$ for all $j$, which is (ii). If (ii) holds, every term with $
u
e0$ in \eqref{eq:taylor} vanishes, which is (iii). Clearly (iii) implies (i). The equality $\widehat U(\mathfrak{t}_n)^\dagger=\widehat U(\mathfrak{h}_n)$ is Lemma~ef{lem:kernel} with $\mathfrak{k}=\mathfrak{h}_n$ and $v_j=t_{0j}$. Finally $F_n(\mathfrak{d}_n)=\mathfrak{d}_n$ because $F_n$ is an automorphism, and $F_n(t_{ij})=t_{n-i,n-j}$ for $0<i,j<n$.
head: environment

label: prop:core
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:core}
Let $n\ge2$. Then
\[
\bigcap_{\sigma\in\Sigma_{n+1}}P_\sigma\bigl(s\,\widehat U(\mathfrak{t}_n)\bigr)=s\,\widehat U(\mathfrak{d}_n),\qquad
\bigcap_{\sigma\in\Sigma_{n+1}}P_\sigma(s\mathfrak{t}_n)=s\mathfrak{d}_n .
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since the framings are central, \eqref{eq:framing-splitting} gives $\overline{[\mathfrak{ft}_n,\mathfrak{ft}_n]}=s\mathfrak{d}_n$. Lie algebra automorphisms preserve closed derived subalgebras, so $P_\sigma(s\mathfrak{d}_n)=s\mathfrak{d}_n$ and $P_\sigma(s\,\widehat U(\mathfrak{d}_n))=s\,\widehat U(\mathfrak{d}_n)\subset s\,\widehat U(\mathfrak{t}_n)$ for all $\sigma$. This proves the inclusions $\supset$.

Conversely, let $s(u)$ lie in the left-hand intersection, so that $P_\sigma s(u)\in s\,\widehat U(\mathfrak{t}_n)$ for all $\sigma\in\Sigma_{n+1}$. Fix $0\le i<n$ and $\pi\in\Sigma_n$ with $\pi(i)=0$. Then $P_{\rho_n}s(P_\pi u)=P_{\rho_n}P_\pi s(u)\in s\,\widehat U(\mathfrak{t}_n)$, so $P_\pi u\in\widehat U(\mathfrak{t}_n)^\dagger$ by Corollary~\ref{cor:dagger}. For $a\ne b$ let $e_{ab}$ extract the weight-one coefficient of $t_{ab}$ and $\partial_{ab}=(e_{ab}\otimes\operatorname{id})\circ\Delta$. Then $P_\pi\partial_{ab}P_\pi^{-1}=\partial_{\pi(a)\pi(b)}$. Hence $\partial_{0k}(P_\pi u)=0$ for $0<k<n$ gives $\partial_{ik}u=0$ for all $k\ne i$. As $i$ is arbitrary, $\partial_{ab}u=0$ for all $a<b$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:kernel} with $\mathfrak{k}=\mathfrak{d}_n$ and $\{v\}=\{t_{ab}\}_{a<b}$ gives $u\in\widehat U(\mathfrak{d}_n)$.

For the Lie statement, $P_\sigma$ and $s$ are morphisms of Hopf algebras, so $P_\sigma(s\mathfrak{t}_n)=P_\sigma(s\,\widehat U(\mathfrak{t}_n))\cap\mathfrak{ft}_n$, and intersecting the first identity with $\mathfrak{ft}_n=\operatorname{Prim}\widehat U(\mathfrak{ft}_n)$ and using $\operatorname{Prim}\widehat U(\mathfrak{d}_n)=\mathfrak{d}_n$ gives the second.
head: environment

label: cor:suboperad
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:suboperad}
The family $s\mathfrak{d}=(s\mathfrak{d}_n)_{n\ge1}$ is a cyclic suboperad of $\mathfrak{ft}$ in complete Lie algebras, and $s\mathfrak{d}_n=\overline{[\mathfrak{ft}_n,\mathfrak{ft}_n]}$. If $(V_n)_{n\ge1}$ is any family of subspaces $V_n\subset s\mathfrak{t}_n$ with $P_\sigma(V_n)=V_n$ for all $\sigma\in\Sigma_{n+1}$, then $V_n\subset s\mathfrak{d}_n$ for all $n$. In particular, $s\mathfrak{d}$ is the largest cyclic suboperad of $\mathfrak{ft}$ contained in $s\mathfrak{t}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The equality $s\mathfrak{d}_n=\overline{[\mathfrak{ft}_n,\mathfrak{ft}_n]}$ was shown in the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:core}. Each $\circ_a\colon\mathfrak{ft}_m\oplus\mathfrak{ft}_k\to\mathfrak{ft}_{m+k-1}$ and each $P_\sigma$ is a continuous Lie algebra map, and the closed derived algebra of $\mathfrak{ft}_m\oplus\mathfrak{ft}_k$ is $s\mathfrak{d}_m\oplus s\mathfrak{d}_k$. Hence $s\mathfrak{d}$ is closed under composition and the cyclic action. If $V_n\subset s\mathfrak{t}_n$ is $\Sigma_{n+1}$-stable, then $V_n=P_\sigma(V_n)\subset P_\sigma(s\mathfrak{t}_n)$ for every $\sigma$, and Proposition~\ref{prop:core} gives $V_n\subset s\mathfrak{d}_n$.
head: environment

label: rem:noquotient
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:noquotient}
The framings cannot be discarded operadically: $qP_{\rho_n}(T_{00})=2c_n\ne0=F_nq(T_{00})$, and $q$ is not a morphism of operads by \eqref{eq:cabling}. The flip is Ihara's action of $\rho_n$ on $\mathfrak{t}_n/\mathbb{K} c_n$ \cite[\S5.3]{ihara_braids}, but $(\mathbb{K} c_n)_n$ is not an operadic ideal, since $c_m\circ_a0=c_{m+k-1}-c_B$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The identity $F_n=qP_{\rho_n}s$ is Proposition~\ref{prop:reflection}(2), and $P_{\rho_n}s=sF_n$ on $\widehat U(\mathfrak{d}_n)$ is Proposition~\ref{prop:reflection}(3). Part (2) is Proposition~\ref{prop:taylor}. The description of $\widehat U(\mathfrak{t}_n)^\dagger$ and the identity $P_{\rho_n}s=sF_n$ on it are Corollary~\ref{cor:dagger}. The intersection formula is Proposition~\ref{prop:core}, and the statement on $s\mathfrak{d}$ is Corollary~\ref{cor:suboperad}.
head: environment

label: prop:pathflip
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:pathflip}
For $\psi\in\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_2'$,
\[
F_4(\psi^{0,1,2})=\psi^{01,2,3},\qquad F_4(\psi^{0,12,3})=\psi^{0,1,23},\qquad F_4(\psi^{1,2,3})=\psi(t_{23},t_{12}),
\]
and the same identities hold for $g\in\exp(\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_2')$. Consequently $F_4(S_\psi)=S'_\psi$ and $F_4(S_g)=S'_g$.
head: environment

label: prop:flipequation
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:flipequation}
For $g\in\exp(\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_2')$ put $C_g=S_g^{-1}F_4(S_g)$. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item $C_g\in\exp(\mathfrak{d}_{123})$.
\item $C_g=g^{1,2,3}$.
\item $g$ satisfies \textup{(P)}.
\item $P_{\rho_4}s(S_g)=s\bigl(S_g\,g^{1,2,3}\bigr)$ in $\widehat U(\mathfrak{ft}_4)$.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover $P_{\rho_4}s(S_g)=s(S'_g)$ for every $g\in\exp(\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_2')$. For $\psi\in\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_2'$ the following are equivalent: \textup{(a$'$)} $(F_4-1)S_\psi\in\mathfrak{d}_{123}$; \textup{(b$'$)} $(F_4-1)S_\psi=\psi^{1,2,3}$; \textup{(c$'$)} $\psi$ satisfies \textup{(P$'$)}; \textup{(d$'$)} $P_{\rho_4}s(S_\psi)=s(S_\psi+\psi^{1,2,3})$.
head: environment
name: The flip equation

title: Proof
body_md:
Each substitution $g^{A,B,C}$ lies in $\exp(\mathfrak{d}_4)$ since $g\in\exp(\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_2')$, so $S_g\in\widehat U(\mathfrak{d}_4)$, and Proposition~\ref{prop:reflection}(3) and Proposition~\ref{prop:pathflip} give $P_{\rho_4}s(S_g)=sF_4(S_g)=s(S'_g)$. Hence $C_g=S_g^{-1}S'_g$, which gives (b)$\Leftrightarrow$(c), and (c)$\Leftrightarrow$(d) because $s$ is injective. Clearly (b)$\Rightarrow$(a). For (a)$\Rightarrow$(b), note that $g(0,v)=1$ for $g\in\exp(\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_2')$, so
\[
\begin{gathered}
\pi_0(S_g)=g(0,t_{12})\,g(0,t_{13}+t_{23})=1,\\
\pi_0(S'_g)=g(t_{12},t_{23})\,g(0,t_{12}+t_{13})=g(t_{12},t_{23}),
\end{gathered}
\]
hence $\pi_0(C_g)=\pi_0(g^{1,2,3})$. Both $C_g$ and $g^{1,2,3}$ lie in $\iota\,\widehat U(\mathfrak{t}_{\{1,2,3\}})$, on which $\pi_0$ is injective, so $C_g=g^{1,2,3}$. The Lie case is identical, with $\pi_0(S_\psi)=0$ and $\pi_0(S'_\psi)=\psi(t_{12},t_{23})$.
head: environment

label: cor:fliplocus
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:fliplocus} We have
\[
\begin{gathered}
\bigl\{g\in\exp(\mathcal{F}^3\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_2):C_g\in\exp(\mathfrak{d}_{123})\bigr\}={\mathsf{GRT}}_1,\\
\bigl\{\psi\in\mathcal{F}^3\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_2:(F_4-1)S_\psi\in\mathfrak{d}_{123}\bigr\}={\mathfrak{grt}}_1 .
\end{gathered}
\]
Without the normalisation, $\{\psi\in\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_2':(F_4-1)S_\psi\in\mathfrak{d}_{123}\}=\mathbb{K}\cdot [x,y]\oplus{\mathfrak{grt}}_1$, and $\{\psi\in\mathbb{K} y\oplus\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_2':(F_4-1)S_\psi\in\mathfrak{d}_{123}\}=\mathbb{K} y\oplus\mathbb{K}\cdot [x,y]\oplus{\mathfrak{grt}}_1$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The first two identities follow from Proposition~\ref{prop:flipequation} and Definition~\ref{def:grt}, and the third from Remark~\ref{rem:normalisation}. For the last, $S_y=t_{12}+t_{13}+t_{23}$ is fixed by $F_4$, so $y$ satisfies the flip condition, and the condition is linear in $\psi$.
head: environment

label: prop:astr
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:astr}
Let $g\in\exp(\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_2)$. Then $P_{\rho_4}s(S_g)\in s\,\widehat U(\mathfrak{t}_4)$ if and only if the coefficient of $x$ in $g$ vanishes. In that case, $P_{\rho_4}s(S_g)=s\bigl(S_g\,h^{1,2,3}\bigr)$ for some $h\in\exp(\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_2')$ if and only if $g=\varphi\exp(\alpha y)$ with $\varphi\in{\mathsf{ASTR}}$ and $\alpha\in\mathbb{K}$, and then $h=\varphi$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: For group-like $u$, $\Delta u=u\otimes u$ gives $\partial_{0j}u=e_{0j}(\log u)\,u$. If $\beta$ and $\alpha$ are the coefficients of $x$ and $y$ in $g$, the weight-one part of $\log S_g$ is $\beta(2t_{01}+t_{02})+\alpha(t_{12}+t_{13}+t_{23})$, so $S_g\in\widehat U(\mathfrak{t}_4)^\dagger$ if and only if $\beta=0$. The first assertion is Corollary~\ref{cor:dagger}, (i)$\Leftrightarrow$(ii). If $\beta=0$, Corollary~\ref{cor:dagger} gives $P_{\rho_4}s(S_g)=sF_4(S_g)$, and since $s$ is injective the second assertion is \cite[Theorem~78(1)]{FHK}, whose proof holds over any field of characteristic zero.
head: environment

label: cor:twocycle
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:twocycle}
Let $g\in\exp(\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_2)$ satisfy \textup{(P)}. Then $g\in\exp(\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_2')$ and $g(x,y)\,g(y,x)=1$. Similarly, if $\psi\in\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_2'$ satisfies \textup{(P$'$)}, then $\psi(x,y)+\psi(y,x)=0$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By \cite[Lemma~75(1)]{FHK}, $g\in\exp(\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_2')$. By Proposition~\ref{prop:flipequation}, $F_4(S_g)=S_g\,g^{1,2,3}$. Apply $F_4$ and use $F_4^2=\operatorname{id}$, which on $\widehat U(\mathfrak{d}_4)$ is the relation $P_{\rho_4}^2=1$ read through $P_{\rho_4}s=sF_4$, together with $F_4(g^{1,2,3})=g(t_{23},t_{12})$:
\[
S_g=F_4\bigl(S_g\,g^{1,2,3}\bigr)=S_g\,g^{1,2,3}\,g(t_{23},t_{12}).
\]
Hence $g(t_{12},t_{23})\,g(t_{23},t_{12})=1$, and injectivity of $x\mapsto t_{12}$, $y\mapsto t_{23}$ on $\widehat U(\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_2)$ gives $g(x,y)g(y,x)=1$. The Lie case is identical.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The first assertion is Proposition~\ref{prop:astr}. If $g$ has no linear term in $x$, write $g=\varphi\exp(\alpha y)$ with $\varphi\in\exp(\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_2')$. Then $g^{A,B,C}=\varphi^{A,B,C}\exp(\alpha t_{BC})$, so Proposition~\ref{prop:pathflip}, $F_4(t_{12})=t_{23}$ and $F_4(t_{13}+t_{23})=t_{12}+t_{13}$ give $F_4(S_g)=S'_g$, and Corollary~\ref{cor:dagger}, (i)$\Rightarrow$(iii), gives $P_{\rho_4}s(S_g)=sF_4(S_g)$. The identification with the flip equation is Proposition~\ref{prop:astr}, and the two-cycle relation is Corollary~\ref{cor:twocycle}.

label: prop:reflectedpentagon
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:reflectedpentagon}
Let $g\in\exp(\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_2')$. The involution $\kappa_4$ fixes $p_0$, exchanges $p_1\leftrightarrow p_4$ and $p_2\leftrightarrow p_3$, and satisfies $\kappa_4(\mathbf{A}_g^{0,1,2})=\mathbf{A}_g^{01,2,3}$ and $\kappa_4(\mathbf{A}_g^{0,12,3})=\mathbf{A}_g^{0,1,23}$. Hence $\alpha_g^{-1}\kappa_4(\alpha_g)\colon p_2\to p_3$ has coefficient $s(C_g)$, and $\alpha_g^{-1}\kappa_4(\alpha_g)=\mathbf{A}_g^{1,2,3}$ if and only if $g$ satisfies \textup{(P)}. In that case $\kappa_4(\mathbf{A}_g^{1,2,3})=(\mathbf{A}_g^{1,2,3})^{-1}$, which is the two-cycle relation.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: As unrooted trees with boundary order $(0,1,2,3,4)$, the $p_i$ are determined by the two-element parts of their splits, $p_0:\{01,34\}$, $p_1:\{12,34\}$, $p_2:\{12,40\}$, $p_3:\{23,40\}$, $p_4:\{01,23\}$, and $\rho_4$ relabels these by $01\leftrightarrow34$, $12\leftrightarrow23$, and $M$ restores the boundary order. On coefficients $\kappa_4$ acts on $s\,\widehat U(\mathfrak{d}_4)$ by $F_4$, so the remaining assertions are Propositions~\ref{prop:pathflip}, \ref{prop:flipequation} and Corollary~\ref{cor:twocycle}.

label: lem:generators
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:generators}
Let $\Theta\in\operatorname{Aut}^+_{\mathbf{Op}}({\mathsf{PaRCD}}_{\mathbb{K}})$. Suppose that $\Theta P_\sigma(z)=P_\sigma\Theta(z)$ for every $z\in\{\exp(\lambda\mathbf{I}),\exp(\lambda\mathbf{H}),\mathbf{X},\mathbf{A}:\lambda\in\mathbb{K}\}$ of arity $m$ and every $\sigma\in\Sigma_{m+1}$. Then $\Theta$ commutes with the whole cyclic action. Moreover, for a morphism $z$ of arity $m$, the condition $\Theta P_\sigma(z)=P_\sigma\Theta(z)$ for all $\sigma\in\Sigma_{m+1}$ holds if and only if $\Theta P_{\tau_m}(P_\pi z)=P_{\tau_m}\Theta(P_\pi z)$ for all $\pi\in\Sigma_m$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For the second assertion, $\Sigma_m$ is the stabiliser of $m$ in $\Sigma_{m+1}$ and acts transitively on $\{0,\dots,m-1\}$, so $\Sigma_{m+1}=\Sigma_m\sqcup\Sigma_m\tau_m\Sigma_m$. As $\Theta$ commutes with $P_\pi$ for $\pi\in\Sigma_m$, for $\sigma=\pi_1\tau_m\pi_2$ we get
\[
\Theta P_\sigma z=P_{\pi_1}\Theta P_{\tau_m}(P_{\pi_2}z)=P_{\pi_1}P_{\tau_m}\Theta(P_{\pi_2}z)=P_\sigma\Theta z
\]
whenever $\Theta$ commutes with $P_{\tau_m}$ on $P_{\pi_2}z$. The converse is clear.

For the first assertion, let $\mathcal M$ be the set of morphisms $z$, of any arity $m$, such that $\Theta P_\sigma z=P_\sigma\Theta z$ for all $\sigma\in\Sigma_{m+1}$. Since $\Theta$ and each $P_\sigma$ are continuous functors, $\mathcal M$ is closed under composition, inverses and limits. If $x,y\in\mathcal M$, then by \eqref{eq:cyclic-equivariance} and since $\Theta$ is an operad morphism,
\begin{align*}
\Theta P_\sigma(x\circ_ay)&=P_\pi\bigl(\Theta P_{\sigma'}x\circ_b\Theta P_{\sigma''}y\bigr)=P_\pi\bigl(P_{\sigma'}\Theta x\circ_bP_{\sigma''}\Theta y\bigr)\\
&=P_\sigma(\Theta x\circ_a\Theta y)=P_\sigma\Theta(x\circ_ay),
\end{align*}
and similarly in the second case of \eqref{eq:cyclic-equivariance}. Thus $\mathcal M$ is closed under operadic composition. It contains the generators by hypothesis, hence all morphisms.

label: lem:injective
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:injective}
Let $u,v$ be two distinct elements of $\{T_{01},T_{12},T_{02}\}\subset\mathfrak{ft}_3$. The continuous algebra map $\widehat U(\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_2)\to\widehat U(\mathfrak{ft}_3)$, $x\mapsto u$, $y\mapsto v$, is injective. In particular $g(u,v)g(v,u)=1$ if and only if $g(x,y)g(y,x)=1$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Let $\mathcal{Z}\subset\mathfrak{ft}_3$ be the central ideal spanned by $T_{00},T_{11},T_{22}$ and $s(c_3)$. By \eqref{eq:framing-splitting} and \cite{Drin}, $\mathfrak{ft}_3/\mathcal{Z}\cong\mathfrak{t}_3/\mathbb{K} c_3$ is freely generated by the classes of $T_{01}$ and $T_{12}$, and the class of $T_{02}$ is $-T_{01}-T_{12}$. Any two of the three classes form a free generating pair, since $(x,y)\mapsto(-x-y,y)$ and $(x,y)\mapsto(x,-x-y)$ are automorphisms of $\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_2$. Hence the composite $\widehat U(\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_2)\to\widehat U(\mathfrak{ft}_3)\to\widehat U(\mathfrak{ft}_3/\mathcal{Z})$ is an isomorphism.
head: environment

label: prop:arity3
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:arity3}
Let $g\in\exp(\widehat{\mathfrak{f}}_2')$. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item $\Theta_gP_\sigma\mathbf{A}=P_\sigma\Theta_g\mathbf{A}$ for every $\sigma\in\Sigma_4$.
\item $\Theta_gP_{\tau_3}\mathbf{A}=P_{\tau_3}\Theta_g\mathbf{A}$.
\item $g(x,y)\,g(y,x)=1$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $\tau=\tau_3$ and $\gamma_{abc}=g(T_{ab},T_{bc})$. Proceeding as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:tau-generators}, one finds
\[
P_\tau A_{012}=A_{120}^{-1},\qquad P_\tau A_{021}=A_{210}^{-1},\qquad P_\tau A_{102}=A_{201}.
\]
For instance, $((10)2)$ has boundary order $(1,0,2,3)$ and split $\{1,0\}\,|\,\{2,3\}$. After relabelling by $(0\,3)$ and re-rooting at $3$ it becomes $((20)1)$, and $(1(02))$ becomes $(2(01))$. Since $P_\tau^2=1$ and $P_\tau$ is a functor, the three remaining cases are $P_\tau A_{120}=A_{012}^{-1}$, $P_\tau A_{210}=A_{021}^{-1}$ and $P_\tau A_{201}=A_{102}$. For $z=A_{abc}$ and $P_\tau z=A_{a'b'c'}^{\epsilon}$ both $\Theta_gP_\tau z$ and $P_\tau\Theta_g z$ have the same source and target, with coefficients $\gamma_{a'b'c'}^{\epsilon}$ and $P_\tau(\gamma_{abc})$, so compatibility on $z$ reads $P_\tau(\gamma_{abc})=\gamma_{a'b'c'}^{\epsilon}$. By \eqref{eq:output},
\[
\begin{gathered}
P_\tau(T_{01})=T_{31}=T_{02}-s(c_3)-T_{11},\quad P_\tau(T_{02})=T_{32}=T_{01}-s(c_3)-T_{22},\\
P_\tau(T_{12})=T_{12},
\end{gathered}
\]
and $s(c_3)+T_{11}$, $s(c_3)+T_{22}$ are central in $\mathfrak{ft}_3$. By \eqref{eq:shift}, applied to each argument:
\begin{itemize}
\item for $z=A_{012}$: $P_\tau(\gamma_{012})=g(T_{02},T_{12})$ and $\gamma_{120}^{-1}=g(T_{12},T_{02})^{-1}$,
\item for $z=A_{021}$: $P_\tau(\gamma_{021})=g(T_{32},T_{12})=g(T_{01},T_{12})$ and $\gamma_{210}^{-1}=g(T_{12},T_{01})^{-1}$,
\item for $z=A_{102}$: $P_\tau(\gamma_{102})=g(T_{31},T_{32})=g(T_{02},T_{01})=\gamma_{201}$.
\end{itemize}
The third condition always holds. By Lemma~\ref{lem:injective}, each of the first two is equivalent to (iii). In particular (ii)$\Leftrightarrow$(iii). Compatibility on $z$ is equivalent to compatibility on $P_\tau z$ and on $z^{-1}$. Hence, if (iii) holds, then $\Theta_g$ commutes with $P_\tau$ on every $P_\pi\mathbf{A}$, $\pi\in\Sigma_3$. The argument for the second assertion of Lemma~\ref{lem:generators} uses only that $\Theta_g$ commutes with $P_\pi$, $\pi\in\Sigma_3$, on the morphisms $A^{\pm1}_{abc}$, which holds by \eqref{eq:thetaext}. Hence (i) holds. Clearly (i)$\Rightarrow$(ii).

label: prop:cyclicity
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:cyclicity}
Let $g\in{\mathsf{GRT}}_1$. The automorphism $\Theta_g$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:classification} lies in the subgroup $\operatorname{Aut}^+_{\mathbf{cyc},1}({\mathsf{PaRCD}}_{\mathbb{K}})$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: We verify the hypothesis of Lemma~\ref{lem:generators}. The restriction of $\Theta_g$ to ${\mathsf{PaRCD}}_{\mathbb{K}}(1)$ and ${\mathsf{PaRCD}}_{\mathbb{K}}(2)$ is the identity. Indeed, ${\mathsf{PaRCD}}_{\mathbb{K}}(1)$ has the single object $(0)$ with automorphism group $\exp(\mathbb{K}\mathbf{I})$. In arity two, the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{ft}_2$ is abelian and spanned by $T_{00}$, $T_{11}$ and $T_{01}$, which at $(01)$ are the insertions $1_\mu\circ_0\mathbf{I}$, $1_\mu\circ_1\mathbf{I}$ and $\mathbf{H}$. These are fixed by $\Theta_g$, hence so is $\operatorname{Aut}((01))=\exp(\mathfrak{ft}_2)$, and so are $\mathbf{X}$ and $\operatorname{Aut}((10))=\mathbf{X}^{-1}\operatorname{Aut}((01))\mathbf{X}$. Since each $P_\sigma$ preserves arity, $\Theta_g$ commutes with the cyclic action on $\exp(\mathbb{K}\mathbf{I})$, $\exp(\mathbb{K}\mathbf{H})$ and $\mathbf{X}$. On $\mathbf{A}$, $g$ satisfies the two-cycle relation by Corollary~\ref{cor:twocycle}, so Proposition~\ref{prop:arity3} applies. Lemma~\ref{lem:generators} now shows that $\Theta_g$ is cyclic.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: This is Proposition~\ref{prop:arity3}. For the final statement, by Proposition~\ref{prop:cyclicity}, $g\mapsto\Theta_g$ maps ${\mathsf{GRT}}_1$ into $\operatorname{Aut}^+_{\mathbf{cyc},1}({\mathsf{PaRCD}}_{\mathbb{K}})\subset\operatorname{Aut}^+_{\mathbf{Op},1}({\mathsf{PaRCD}}_{\mathbb{K}})$, and by Theorem~\ref{thm:classification} and equation~\eqref{eq:grouplaw} it is a group isomorphism onto $\operatorname{Aut}^+_{\mathbf{Op},1}({\mathsf{PaRCD}}_{\mathbb{K}})$. Hence $\operatorname{Aut}^+_{\mathbf{cyc},1}({\mathsf{PaRCD}}_{\mathbb{K}})=\operatorname{Aut}^+_{\mathbf{Op},1}({\mathsf{PaRCD}}_{\mathbb{K}})$.
